item.description: • The keyboard backlight stays quiet. With automatic keyboard brightness on, the light sensor adjusts the backlight by tiny amounts several times a second, and 0.14.0 announced every one of them in the notch. Now it shows only when you change the backlight yourself.

• Shuffle and repeat. Both sit beside the play controls. Optionally, a new song's cover slides out of the notch for a moment when the track changes.
  • Small things, announced. Caps Lock, microphone mute, the keyboard backlight, low battery and Low Power Mode each get a brief note in the notch, drawn like the volume display.
  • Stopwatch and focus sessions. The timer has three modes now, and several running things can share the notch instead of the newest replacing the rest. Your next event can count down for its last ten minutes, if you turn that on.
  • A clipboard you can pin and search. Pin up to six entries, search everything you copied, and keep formatting when you copy back (⌥-click for plain text). History, pins included, still never touches the disk.
  • Compress and convert from the shelf. Right-click a file to zip it, or an image to change its format. The result is written next to the original, and the original is left alone.
  • The next line of lyrics. Click the lyric to see the line that's coming as well as the one being sung.
  • The notch on every display (off by default). Each screen gets its own, and the panel opens on whichever one you're using.
  • Out of the way when it should be. While an app is full screen, the pointer no longer opens the panel. Apps you choose in Settings → General get the same treatment even in a window. Esc closes the panel, and ⌃⌥N gives it keyboard focus.
  • Updates in one click. AloeNotch now updates itself through Sparkle: see what changed, click Install, and it reopens on the new version. Every update is signed and checked before it opens. Nothing installs without your click.
  • Motion, refined. The panel can change its mind halfway through opening or closing without a jump, ignores the pointer brushing past on its way to the menu bar, and closes without ever overshooting the notch.
  • Easier to read and use. Text and icons follow Increase Contrast, modules show when they are loading or need a permission instead of sitting blank, and Settings is tidier and ready to be translated.
